severity_criteria.source_excerpt: protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria: "2." "Must have achieved at least 1 of the following 2 treatment success criteria:" "Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) = 0 or 1 (clear or almost clear) at week 16 OR Eczema Area and Severity Index \>= 75% (EASI-75) (at least 75% reduction in EASI score from baseline to week 16)" "IGA is an assessment scale used to determine severity of AD and clinical response to treatment on a 5-point scale (0 = clear; 1 = almost clear; 2 = mild; 3 = moderate; 4 = severe) based on erythema and papulation/infiltration." -- These are alternative prior-study response eligibility routes, not cumulative criteria: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16 OR at least 75% reduction in EASI from baseline to Week 16. The current study requires completion of one of the two named parent studies and does not state a new moderate-to-severe threshold; severity_label is therefore null. Sponsor protocol identifiers are copied from the CT.gov eligibility text.

value.population_note: The registry title and brief summary describe the dupilumab regimens as monotherapy. No concomitant medication policy or background topical agent regimen is specified in the selected registry text.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: protocolSection.identificationModule.officialTitle and descriptionModule.briefSummary: "R668-AD-1415" "A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study Investigating the Efficacy and Safety of Multiple Dupilumab Dose Regimens Administered as Monotherapy for Maintaining Treatment Response in Patients With Atopic Dermatitis" "The primary objective of the study was to assess the ability of different Dupilumab dose regimens, administered as monotherapy, to maintain the treatment response achieved after 16 weeks of initial treatment with Dupilumab monotherapy compared to placebo." "Subcutaneous injection of Dupilumab 300 mg alternatively with placebo (matched to Dupilumab) was administered." -- Monotherapy is explicit in the official title and brief summary. The empty agent and concomitant lists reflect that no such agents or policies are specified in the source text, not an inference that concomitant treatment was prohibited.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: resultsSection.outcomeMeasuresModule.outcomeMeasures[0].analyses[0..2].groupDescription: "NCT02395133" "A 2-sided hierarchical testing procedure was used for the co-primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints in a pre-specified order." "The hierarchical testing sequence continued only when the previous endpoint was statistically significant at 0.05 level." "The hierarchical testing sequence continued only when the previous endpoint was statistically significant at 0.05 level." "Difference Between Current Study Baseline and Week 36 in Percent Change in EASI From Parent Study Baseline (NCT02277743 and NCT02277769)" "Baseline (Parent Study), Baseline (Current Study) and Week 36 (Current study)" "Percentage of Participants With Eczema Area and Severity Index >= 75% [EASI-75] at Baseline of Current Study Maintaining EASI-75 at Week 36" "Week 36" -- The registry reports two-sided hierarchical testing for co-primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints in a prespecified order, continuing only when the previous endpoint was significant at 0.05. study_schedule.source_excerpt: armGroups, outcomesModule, resultsSection.adverseEventsModule.timeFrame: "NCT02395133" "Subcutaneous injection of Placebo (for Dupilumab) was administered once weekly (QW) from Week 1 (Day 1) to Week 36." "Subcutaneous injection of Dupilumab 300 milligram (mg) alternatively with placebo (matched to Dupilumab) was administered once every eight week (Q8W) from Week 1 to Week 36." "Subcutaneous injection of Dupilumab 300 mg alternatively with placebo (matched to Dupilumab) was administered once every four week (Q4W) from Week 1 to Week 36." "Subcutaneous injection of Dupilumab 300 mg alternatively with placebo (matched to Dupilumab) was administered once every week (QW) or twice a week (Q2W) from Week 1 to Week 36." "Baseline (Parent Study), Baseline (Current Study) and Week 36 (Current study)" "Week 36" "Well-controlled weeks are those in which participants during their weekly IVRS call completion has their eczema been well-controlled over the last week during which no rescue treatments were administered." "All Adverse Events (AEs) were collected from signature of the informed consent form up to the final visit (Week 36) regardless of seriousness or relationship to investigational product." -- CT.gov arm descriptions say treatment ran from Week 1 (Day 1 for placebo) to Week 36; outcomes are assessed at Week 36 and the adverse-event time frame calls Week 36 the final visit. Weekly IVRS calls are described for well-controlled weeks, but exact call weeks are not specified. No full per-visit schedule table is present in the cited CT.gov file; screening and any post-treatment follow-up interval are not specified. Whole-trial duration is stated through the Week 36 final visit.

value.rationale: For the Week 36 primary EASI-75 analysis, values after first rescue treatment were set to missing and patients with a missing Week 36 value were considered non-responders. This supports rescued subjects being counted as non-responders for that endpoint only; the supplied registry text does not state rescue permission, trigger, rescue agents, or a broader treatment-failure rule.

published_results.source_excerpt: FDA label section 14.1, SOLO CONTINUE: "Subjects in SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 who had an IGA 0 or 1 with a reduction of ≥2 points were re-randomized into SOLO CONTINUE (NCT02395133)." "SOLO CONTINUE evaluated multiple DUPIXENT monotherapy dose regimens for maintaining treatment response." "The study included subjects randomized to continue with DUPIXENT 300 mg Q2W (62 subjects) or switch to placebo (31 subjects) for 36 weeks." "IGA 0 or 1 responses at Week 36 were as follows: 33 (53%) in the Q2W group and 3 (10%) in the placebo group." -- Label section 14.1 names NCT02395133 and says the 31-person placebo group switched from prior DUPIXENT response into the 36-week continuation trial; the Week 36 IGA 0-or-1 outcome had 3 responders (10%). This row maps to the matching placebo arm OG000 in base.json. The label's Q2W subgroup is not joined to the pooled active OG003 arm because the label subgroup does not uniquely map to that pooled CT.gov arm.
